title: Release audit: --uninstall no longer honors FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE. The old code removed the block
summary: Add ${FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE:-} to the uninstall candidate set when it is set (deduplicate against PROFILE_NAMES), and add a test that installs and uninstalls with a custom profile path.
requirements: R1: When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` is set and non-empty, `--uninstall` removes the marked block from that exact path in addition to the files in `PROFILE_NAMES`.

R2: Removal from the override file is byte-exact between `MARKER_START='# >>> forgel-code >>>'` and `MARKER_END='# <<< forgel-code <<<'`; every line outside the block is preserved in order and no new line is appended by an uninstall.
R3: When `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` is unset or empty, `--uninstall` behaves exactly as before: the six standard profile files under `$HOME` are cleaned and the exit status and output are unchanged.
R4: When the override path does not exist, or exists without the start marker, `--uninstall` still exits 0, prints no error for it and creates no file at that path.

R5: When the override path is the same file as one of the standard profile names under `$HOME` (for example `$HOME/.profile`), the file is cleaned exactly once, loses no non-block content, and the run still exits 0.

R6: A block written into the override profile by a completed install is removed by `--uninstall`; a block left behind by an install that wrote the profile but failed its fresh-shell verification and exited non-zero is removed by the same `--uninstall` invocation.

R7: `tests/test_install.py` gains tests, using the real script and a temporary `$HOME`, that cover: override block removed after a successful install, override block removed after a failed install, override-free run unchanged, and missing override file tolerated.

R8: `README.md` states that the uninstall also removes the marked block from the profile named by `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE`; the documentation stays valid under the existing README guard tests (exactly one install command, one update line, one uninstall line, no extra installation path).
R9: `CHANGELOG.md` carries the fix under an `## [Unreleased]` heading with a `### Fixed` entry, keeping the existing `[0.1.0]` section intact.
R10: The whole repository suite passes: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
acceptance: AC1: With `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` pointing at a file in the temporary `$HOME` that holds the exact marked block plus surrounding lines, `sh install.sh --uninstall` exits 0, the block is gone and the other lines are unchanged (R1, R2).
AC2: With `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` unset, a marked block in `$HOME/.profile` is still removed and `--uninstall` exits 0 (R3).
AC3: With `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` pointing at a nonexistent file, `--uninstall` exits 0 and that file is still absent afterwards; a marker-free existing file keeps its content (R4).
AC4: With `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` set to `$HOME/.profile`, the uninstall leaves `.profile` free of the block and of any other change, exit 0 (R5).
AC5: The new suite tests show the override profile cleaned after both a successful and a failed install (R6, R7).
AC6: `README.md` documents the override-profile cleanup and the README guard tests still pass (R8).
AC7: `CHANGELOG.md` records the fix under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` (R9).
AC8: The full suite `python -m unittest discover -s tests` passes (R10).
plan_goal: Fix install.sh so a new terminal finds forgel-code on PATH

result.summary:
Restored FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE handling in install.sh's --uninstall path and documented/tested it.

Changes:
- install.sh: extracted the per-file cleanup into `uninstall_profile`, kept the six standard `PROFILE_NAMES` loop, and added an additional cleanup of `$FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` when it is set and non-empty. The override cleanup reuses `remove_profile_block`, so removal stays byte-exact against the two markers, preserves all other lines, is a silent no-op for missing/marker-free files, never creates a file, and runs after the standard loop so an override naming `$HOME/.profile` is cleaned exactly once. Exit codes and output are unchanged apart from the extra `Removed the PATH block from ...` line when the override file really carried a block.
- tests/test_install.py: new `InstallerProfileOverrideUninstallTest` (7 tests) running the real `install.sh` under a temporary `$HOME`: override block removed with surrounding lines intact, override block removed after a real successful install, override block removed after an install that wrote the profile and failed its fresh-shell check, standard-profile cleanup unchanged with the variable unset, missing override file tolerated (exit 0, no file created), marker-free override untouched, and an override naming `$HOME/.profile` cleaned exactly once.
- README.md: the Uninstall paragraph and the `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` option row now state that the uninstall also removes the marked block from the profile that variable names, including a block left by an install that failed its fresh-shell check; missing/marker-free files are left alone.
- CHANGELOG.md: added `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` entry above the untouched `[0.1.0]` section.

Testing: `python -m unittest discover -s tests` — 178 tests, OK (includes the README guard tests and `sh -n install.sh`). The focused run `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_install.py` — 30 tests, OK.
assumptions: The override cleanup runs after the six standard names and reuses the same `remove_profile_block` helper, so a duplicate path (e.g. FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE=$HOME/.profile) is rewritten once and reported once; the install-time add_profile_block semantics were not touched.
The override is only cleaned when FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE is set and non-empty; no extra profile is guessed beyond the six standard names, matching the assumption recorded in the specification.

The failed-install scenario is reproduced with a custom (non-shell-read) profile path, which makes the installer write the block and then exit non-zero on the fresh-shell verification, leaving the block for the uninstall to clean.

review.summary: The attributed commit restores override-profile cleanup in `install.sh --uninstall`: a new `uninstall_profile` helper (missing/non-regular file and marker-free file are silent no-ops, removal failure sets status=1) is reused for the six `PROFILE_NAMES` and, when `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` is set and non-empty, for that exact path as an additive second step. The refactor preserves the previous standard-name behavior byte for byte, tolerates duplicates (second call sees no marker), does not create files, and keeps the POSIX `sh` contract. `tests/test_install.py` gains an `InstallerProfileOverrideUninstallTest` class exercising the real script under a temporary `$HOME`: override cleanup, a successful install through an override, a failed-install leftover, override-free run, missing override, marker-free override, and an override naming `$HOME/.profile` cleaned exactly once. README documents the override cleanup in both the Options table and the Uninstall paragraph, and CHANGELOG records the fix under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Fixed` above the intact `[0.1.0]` section. No tests were removed or weakened; QA reports all deterministic checks (AC1-AC5, `sh -n`, full suite) green. Only minor, non-blocking observation: the commit subject is the runtime-generated task title rather than an imperative sentence; this is pipeline bookkeeping, not a product defect.

requirements.requirement: R1: With `FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE` set and non-empty, `--uninstall` removes the marked block from that exact path in addition to `PROFILE_NAMES`.
